subject: COPPA & children's-data attestation request - KidsApp
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@kidsapp.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: COPPA & children's data attestation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday on the product call. As we work toward security review for our new kids product, Legal has asked us to get a short, written attestation from platform vendors about how they treat children's data and prohibited uses. Specifically we need answers on:

- Whether Redwood processes "personal information" of children under 13 when a customer (controller) uses the hosted API (clarify processor vs controller responsibilities).
- Confirmation of platform controls that support age-gating / assent flows (KV cache retention, prefix masking, logs retention).
- Any built-in facilities for verifiable parental consent or specific guidance you provide to customers.
- Whether Redwood will affirm in writing that it will not use data submitted via tenant APIs for training/verbatim retention for customers that opt out (we have a DPA requirement).
- A statement on prohibited uses (e.g., targeted advertising to minors) and whether Redwood enforces those at the platform level or relies on customer policies.

We've attached our questionnaire (KidsApp-Questionnaire.pdf). Can you provide a short attestation and any supporting documents (current DPA/SCCs, SOC 2 evidence pointers) by next week? If it's easier, a one-paragraph attestation plus a pointer to the DPA would be perfect.

Best,
Helen
Head of Privacy, KidsApp
[Attachment: KidsApp-Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)]

Neha: can you own coordination with the customer? Marissa: can you draft an attestation with the compliance language we already use (SOC 2 / processor statements)? Rachel: please review for legal nuance — we should make clear the boundary between Redwood (processor) and customer (controller).

I think a 2-3 sentence attestation + a short FAQ bullet list will close this. Target to Helen: EOD Mon (14th).

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: COPPA & children's data attestation

Karthik / Neha / Rachel —

Draft attestation below (first pass). I pulled language from our standard processor statement and SOC 2 report summary. Please flag any legal redlines.

DRAFT ATTESTATION (for review)
Redwood Inference provides an inference platform and operates as a data processor on behalf of its customers. Redwood does not knowingly direct customers' data collection practices. Redwood does not use customer prompt or result data to retrain models when a customer has opted out via contractually agreed DPA terms. Our hosting and runtime controls are designed to support customers implementing age-gating and parental consent flows: configurable KV-cache retention, request-scoped ephemeral keys, and log retention settings help limit persistent storage of user-submitted content. Redwood does not provide built-in verifiable parental-consent mechanics; customers are responsible for collecting consent and configuring their integration accordingly. Redwood prohibits the use of platform-provided data for targeted advertising to minors and will enforce platform-level restrictions where the activity is within Redwood's control (e.g., marketing data pipelines).

Quick FAQ bullets to include in the packet:
- SOC 2: report available under NDA; SOC 2 scope covers our control environment.
- DPA & SCCs: standard template attached; we can negotiate sections on training/use of customer data.
- Data retention: per-customer retention settings exist; default logs retention is 30 days for request metadata and configurable for customers on Dedicated/Private.
- Responsibility split: controller (customer) = collection/consent. Redwood = secure processing and is willing to add contractual protections.

Attestation doc attached: kidsapp_attestation_draft.docx

Marissa
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kidsapp_attestation_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DRAFT ATTESTATION / DPA redlines

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A couple of legal clarifications and a short polished paragraph I'd recommend sending to the customer: one, emphasize we are a processor and do not have insight into why a customer collects data; two, confirm contractual options to opt-out of use for training; three, avoid absolute statements about enforcement of prohibited uses that are outside our visibility.

Suggested final paragraph for the attestation packet:
"Redwood Inference is a data processor that provides inference services to its customers. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children on behalf of our customers; control of collection, including any age-verification or parental-consent mechanics, rests with the customer as the data controller. Under our standard DPA, customers may contractually opt out of Redwood using customer-submitted content for model training. Redwood applies platform controls (configurable data retention, request-scoped ephemeral keys, and tenant-level logging controls) to limit persistence of input and output data; however, customers are responsible for implementing front-end age-gating and verifiable parental-consent. Redwood will not use customer data for targeted advertising to minors; where feasible we apply automated safeguards to block known advertising pipelines."
I attached a redline of the DPA where we'd add explicit language on training opt-out and retention. Please review the redlines and finalize.

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_redline.pdf (application/pdf)]

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find below our formal attestation and supporting docs attached. Rachel has approved the final wording and we've attached a redline of the DPA that includes an explicit training opt-out clause. If you need a signed copy of the attestation we can countersign and DocuSign the short statement.

FINAL ATTESTATION
Redwood Inference is a data processor providing inference services to its customers. Redwood does not knowingly collect personal information from children on behalf of our customers; control of collection, including any age-verification or parental-consent mechanics, rests with the customer (data controller). Under our standard DPA, customers may contractually opt out of Redwood using customer-submitted content for model training. Redwood applies platform controls (configurable data retention, request-scoped ephemeral keys, and tenant-level logging controls) that help customers limit the persistence of input and output data. Redwood does not provide a built-in verifiable parental-consent flow and expects customers to implement age gating and consent collection. Redwood will not use customer data for targeted advertising to minors and will include contractual language to that effect in the DPA when requested.

Attachments included:
- DPA_redline.pdf (contains proposed contract language on training opt-out and retention)
- kidsapp_attestation_draft.docx (editable attestation for your records)
- signed_attestation.pdf (brief signed statement; awaiting countersignature if you need it formally executed)
